lead.headline: City trials car-free Sundays as cafés spill onto the streets
lead.standfirst: A made-up story to show how the front page looks: the lead gets a big headline, a short summary, and around 250 words across two columns.
body: This is a sample edition of the paper, so none of these stories are real. The lead story sits at the top of the front page, where a real edition puts the most important news of the morning, chosen from the reader's interests and written fresh in plain English.

In this pretend version of events, the council closed six streets to cars for a whole Sunday. Cafés put tables in the road, a brass band played outside the library, and children chalked a hopscotch grid that ran for almost a hundred metres.

Shopkeepers were split. A bakery owner said she sold out of cinnamon buns by eleven, while a hardware shop said trade was slower than usual because customers couldn't park outside. Bus drivers reported smoother journeys on the routes that skirted the closed roads.

The council says it will publish figures on air quality, footfall and bus times before deciding whether to repeat the trial each month. A public meeting is planned for next week, and an online survey stays open until the end of the month.

A real edition would finish here with what happens next and where the story came from. The source line under the headline tells the reader which outlet reported it, so they can read more if they want to.
